title: Caching API Client
prompt:
Write `createClient(fetchImpl)` — an API client with:

- `get(url)` — uses a per-client cache: the first call fetches and caches the PROMISE; repeat calls return the same promise (one flight per URL until invalidated)
- `invalidate(url)` — drops the cache entry for that URL (next `get` re-fetches)
- `invalidateAll()` — clears everything
- `post(url, body)` — never cached; sends `{ method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(body), headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }` and resolves with the parsed response
- all fetches go through the injected `fetchImpl(url, opts)`

tests.name: get dedupes and caches per URL
tests.hint: Same pattern as the checkpoint loader — cache the promise, not the value.

tests.name: invalidate forces a refetch
tests.hint: Map.delete(url) for invalidate; clear() for invalidateAll.

tests.name: post is never cached and sends JSON
tests.hint: post bypasses the cache entirely; build opts with method/body/headers then parse res.json().
